subject.title: fix(acp): exec approvals target the matching concurrent prompt

question: Should structured ACP exec approval events treat a present toolCallId as authoritative—relaying only to a unique matching execute tool call and otherwise failing closed—while retaining session-only fallback solely when the identifier is omitted?
rationale: This determines which concurrent ACP interaction receives a host-execution authorization prompt; tests establish the implementation, but repository history does not independently establish the permanent policy for contradictory or unmatched identifiers.

options.title: Approve authoritative matching
options.body: Accept the PR's least-privilege rule, preserve the omitted-ID compatibility fallback, and land after exact-head validation.

options.title: Require direct run correlation
options.body: Revise the event contract to propagate an originating run identifier and route by that identifier rather than relying on the pending execute-tool map.

recommendation.title: Approve authoritative matching
recommendation.body: Accept the PR's least-privilege rule, preserve the omitted-ID compatibility fallback, and land after exact-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP approval relay and therefore have the clearest history-backed context for its routing and compatibility contract.
